_: V90Phase3Modulator::generateDIL and the boundary search it inlines,
THE SYMBOL IS CALLERLESS IN THE BLOB -- zero relocations name it -- so
the only thing that can score these rows is a test that calls the `ref_`
alias directly.  t_v90dilgen does; t_v90p3mod reaches the same code only
through the two generators that inline it, which is why this set is
registered against the new binary and not against that one.
`updateCodeSegment` is the file-static standing in for the blob's inlined
`updateCodeSegmentPointer`.  Its rows are here rather than in v90p3mod
because generateDIL is now its only caller: grep the file for
`updateCodeSegment(` and there is one call site.  Its anchors carry the
`m->` prefix, which is what keeps them distinct from the textually
identical search at the end of `resetDILGenerator`.
The return type is not mangled and `int` is a claim derived from the
object's `neg %ecx ; movswl %cx,%edi ; mov %edi,%eax`, so it gets rows of
its own: a narrower return and a wider intermediate both change bits the
low sixteen cannot show, and the test compares all thirty-two.

why: EQUIVALENT, and the argument is about the code rather than about the test.  Widening the DECLARATION alone cannot change a value: every assignment to `level` is already a `short` -- `segmentLevel[...]`, `dilLevel[...]` and the explicitly cast `(short)-level` -- so an `int level` holds exactly the values a `short level` holds, and `return level` returns the same number.  The 16-bit wrap the object encodes as `neg %ecx ; movswl %cx,%edi` lives in the CAST, not in the declaration; the row `the negated level is not wrapped back into sixteen bits` moves the value that the cast protects and IS caught.

why: EQUIVALENT over every value the operands can take, which is why the object's `jle` is a codegen fact and not a behavioural one (the finding-613 class).  `level` is a sixteen-bit ZERO extension, so it is 0..65535 and non-negative in thirty-two bits; every entry of the table is 124..32768 and positive.  Signed and unsigned comparison differ only when one operand has its top bit set, and neither ever does, so the two spellings agree over the whole domain.  The row that DOES bite is `the boundary search reads the level as a signed short`, which makes the level negative and is caught.
